description.value: The study examined sex-based differences in BOLD neural responses to high- versus low-energy-dense food cues in obese men and women under fed and fasted conditions, using visual and auditory stimuli.

spans.text: Using BOLD whole-brain functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), we sought to elucidate the effect of gender on neural responsivity to high vs. low energy-dense (ED) food cues with visual and auditory modalities in fed and fasted conditions.

value: We hypothesized that obese women (vs. men) would have higher neural activation in emotion-related regions in response to external food stimuli.
